data.title: DOM VIRUS launches with 10 games
data.subtitle: Your page. Their playground.
lead: DOM VIRUS launches with ten tiny arcade games that play on a real webpage. Letters become points, buttons become enemy factories, and Recall gives the page back. No install to play. Every game is open source under the MIT licence.

blocks.heading: One maker, a game a week

body.text: DOM VIRUS is made by one person, Chris Cooley, a game a week on the side.
Play it here, then make it part of your own project. Visit GitHub for the source code, setup instructions, and integration examples.

items.title: Sherman Bytes
items.body: A pixel tank on a live webpage. Breach button bases, build cover, hold the page.

items.title: DOM Battlefield
items.body: Squad tactics. Command up to twelve Sherman tanks on a grid built from real page elements.

items.title: Battlefield Blitz
items.body: Every tank for itself. Parachute in, call airstrikes, most kills in three minutes wins.

items.title: Swarm Protocol
items.body: Bugs eat letters into binary and drain your buttons. Squash them before the interface falls apart.

items.title: Byte Runner
items.body: A round pixel frog races through food pipes, eats real text and hunts escaping flies.

items.title: Null Invaders
items.body: Fly an interceptor through a real webpage. Break the button factories and clear the aliens they release.

items.title: DOM Kaiju
items.body: TO CONFIRM. A giant pixel gorilla climbs your page from the footer to the top, smashing as he goes.

items.title: DOM Crossfire
items.body: TO CONFIRM. The DOM VIRUS hero meets the Battlefield arena: interceptor and tank against everything.

items.title: DOM Flock
items.body: TO CONFIRM. Pixel birds burst out of the page in pairs. You are the crosshair.

items.title: Game ten
items.body: TO CONFIRM. Name and one line from the owner before this post is scheduled.
